stamp_note: newest stamp inside the chains, not a clock read — verify() is run by CI and its output is drift-checked, so it must not depend on when it ran

k17_resolution.question: is data/app/ledger/ledger.jsonl verifiable, and what is its entry_hash recipe?
k17_resolution.finding: the hash is over the PAIR {prev, body} produced by chain_hash() in scripts/pick_ledger.py, not over the body alone — which is why hashing the body under four canonicalisations never reproduced it. The recipe is documented in the writer and CI already runs `python3 scripts/pick_ledger.py verify`, which passes. Note for anyone re-deriving this: a SETTLED entry carries payload_sha256 but no payload of its own — it copies the hash of the publish entry it grades — so re-hashing its body is a false alarm, not tampering. This session's first verifier made exactly that mistake and reported 9 problems before the kind check was added.
k17_resolution.conclusion: K-17 resolved as a documentation gap, not a linkage break. No entry was re-hashed and no file in another session's tree was modified.
